date.label: Undated narrative of the southern campaign
date.note: Biblical narrative chronology is not independently established as an absolute BCE date.

claims.claim: Five allied kings attack Gibeon; Jerusalem’s king is one of five (Joshua 10:1–5)
Five defeated kings are recovered from cave at Makkedah (Joshua 10:16–27)
Joshua 10 attributes celestial intervention and quotes Book of Jashar (Joshua 10:12–14)
Horam of Gezer intervenes; text does not say Gezer taken then (Joshua 10:33)

connections.note: The oath sworn to Gibeon in Joshua 9:15–27 explains both the rescue request and the warfare that follows in Joshua 10.
Habakkuk 3:11 shares the celestial imagery of Joshua 10 as poetic divine-combat language, not as a direct record of the same event.
2 Samuel 1:18 also refers to the Book of Jashar, confirming the literary name of a work whose contents do not survive.
Judges 1:8–10 describes related southern campaigns, but they differ in agent and event from Joshua 10, so no identity between them is asserted.
